subject: ZenHealth BYO KMS onboarding, rotation cadence, and HSM evidence
messages:
From: Emma Foster <emma.foster@zenhealth.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood-inference.com
Cc: procurement@zenhealth.com, security@zenhealth.com, devops@zenhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-22T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: BYO key onboarding and rotation — initial evidence request

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we move toward technical due diligence for ZenHealth's procurement review, our security team asked for a concise packet describing Redwood's BYO (customer-supplied key) onboarding flow, HSM integration evidence, and your key rotation procedures (both customer-controlled BYOK and Redwood-managed keys).

High-level items we need by EOD Wednesday (2026-11-25):
- Step-by-step BYOK onboarding checklist for customer ops (including any CLI/API and required artifacts).
- Evidence of HSM attestation or summary for the HSM models Redwood uses when offering managed keys.
- Rotation policy details: recommended cadence, supported forced-rotation processes, and key compromise playbook.
- TLS bindings: how customer key material is used (or not) in TLS mutual auth endpoints and cipher suites supported.
- Any constraints for zero-downtime rotation (prefix caching, KV cache invalidation notes).

If you have a single combined artifact (PDF + short annexes) that would be ideal. Let me know if you need a short extension.

Thanks,
Emma Foster
Director, Security Engineering
ZenHealth
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood-inference.com>
To: Emma Foster <emma.foster@zenhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@zenhealth.com, security@zenhealth.com, devops@zenhealth.com, marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com, karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2026-11-22T11:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: BYO key onboarding and rotation — initial evidence request

Emma —

Appreciate the clear ask. We've pulled together a compact packet that answers each bullet and includes pragmatic operational notes for zero-downtime rotation. Attaching three short artifacts: 1) Redwood BYO Onboarding Checklist (PDF), 2) HSM Attestation Summary (PDF), and 3) TLS cipher/capability matrix (CSV). A quick summary below; the attachments have the full answers and evidence.

Summary — key points:
- BYO onboarding: customer uploads a wrapped key blob via our secure onboarding API (or SFTP for large HSM export formats). We support PKCS#8 wrapped with AES-KW and recommend uploading an HSM-wrapped key when using hardware modules. Customer retains cleartext key material; Redwood stores only an envelope-wrapped key under customer-specific encrypting key.
- HSM evidence: we use FIPS 140-2 Level 3 and Level 4 certified modules from two vendors (listed in the attestation). We include vendor attestation docs and the serial range hashes we saw during onboarding tests.
- Rotation: recommended cadence is 90–180 days for most regulated workloads; we support forced rotation via API with a staged rollout. Rotation is implemented as: create new key version -> provision to runtime -> drain KV cache per-instance -> switch active alias -> retire old versions after retention window. We document TTLs and warm-up steps to avoid tokenization/response regressions.
- TLS: KEKs are not used directly for TLS leaf certificates on public endpoints. For mutual-TLS (mTLS) integrations where customers supply certs, we support binding to a customer-managed key through a customer-controlled private key uploaded to their VPC/private deployment; hosted endpoints use server-side certs managed by Redwood and do not have customer private key material. Cipher suites supported include TLS1.2/TLS1.3 preferred: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 plus RSA/ECDSA fallbacks — see attached CSV.
- Zero-downtime: we provide a prefix/KV cache invalidation API that can be called per-deployment. Typical warm-up: provision new key -> send synthetic traffic to warm caches -> flip alias. Our default traffic drain window is configurable (30–300s) depending on latency SLO.

Next steps:
- I've attached the evidence. If you want, we can run a short hands-on BYO onboarding session (30–45m) with your devops to walk through an actual wrapped key upload.

Attachments (sent): redwood_byo_onboarding_checklist.pdf, hsm_attestation_summary.pdf, tls_cipher_matrix.csv

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Senior Security Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Soojin — that summary helps. A couple of follow-ups from our security team after reviewing the packet:

1) For the HSM attestation PDF: can you provide the explicit model numbers and firmware-minimum versions you tested with? Our procurement needs this to match our vendor whitelist.

2) For the forced-rotation playbook: can you clarify how active requests that are mid-KV-cache (e.g., long-running streaming responses) are handled? Is there an automatic fallback to the old key material or do you quiesce those streams?

3) For mTLS in Hosted scenario: we need a short diagram showing where customer key material sits when using Redwood Private vs Redwood Hosted (one-page). Can you produce that?

If those three items are available Monday morning (2026-11-24), we can close the compliance checklist and move to contract signatures.

Best,
Emma
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>

Date: 2026-11-24T14:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: BYO key onboarding and rotation — initial evidence request

Emma —

Following up from Soojin's thread. Quick answers to each of your follow-ups and links to the one-page diagram and firmware matrix: 

1) HSM models and tested firmware: we have validated onboarding with the following modules and minimum firmware (covered in attached hsm_attestation_summary.pdf, excerpt below):
- VendorA Luna 7910 (fw >= 5.3.1)
- VendorB Thales nShield Connect 6000 (fw >= 2.1.4)
- VendorC SafeNet Luna Network HSM 7.x (fw >= 7.2.0)

2) Long-running streaming requests: streaming tokens reference an internal session that includes a pointer to the active key version. During forced rotation we keep the old key version available for active sessions for a configurable grace window (default 600s). New sessions use the new key. For safety, if a compromise is suspected we can immediately revoke old versions and abort sessions — that is a manual escalation and we will coordinate with your security contact (we document the steps).

3) Diagram and where keys live: hosted flow: customer uploads wrapped key -> Redwood stores envelope-wrapped blob in tenant namespace (cryptographic boundary within Redwood control plane) -> runtime retrieves wrapped blob and unwraps in HSM-backed key cache (customer material never written to disk unencrypted). Private/VPC flow: customer keys can remain in customer KMS/HSM; Redwood runtime in the VPC uses an evicted short-lived session to reference the customer KMS via SPI (no key material leaves the VPC). One-page PDF link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1diagram_byo_hosted_private/view

We can also schedule the hands-on onboarding session tomorrow; Soojin or I can lead. Let me know which time slot works; we'll block 45 minutes.

Sincerely,
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
